headline: Washington Park and Grand Boulevard give Ward 3 deep history and a tough rental market.
summary:
Ward 3 stretches across Douglas, Washington Park, Grand Boulevard, and the Near South Side. Its 44.67 score lands it 29th of 50, squarely in the middle of the pack. Preservation and city responsiveness carry the ward's best marks. Thirty one properties here made it onto the National Register of Historic Places, while a separate 35 hold official Chicago Landmark status, both counts running higher than most of the fifty, and 33 mapped parks put the ward in third place on green space. City crews respond quickly too, with rodent-baiting calls closing in just under three days and street-light repairs wrapped up in well under two, another top-three turnaround time in Chicago.

Housing tells a different story. Eighty five percent of residential parcels here list a taxpayer address that does not match the property itself, the largest share among Chicago's fifty wards, a strong signal of landlord and investor ownership rather than owner-occupancy. A separate estimate finds landlords keeping roughly 70 cents of every rent dollar collected here as profit rather than mortgage payoff, a mark that trails most of the city. The ward's houses of worship also span a narrower range of religious traditions than most other wards. Put together, Ward 3 carries one of the city's stronger preservation and civic records inside a housing market that leans heavily toward landlords.
reading_the_rankings:
Two of these rankings need a second look beyond the raw number. The ward's National Register count places 2nd, but that 2nd place is measured against just 41 wards with usable data, not the complete set of fifty, so it is a high mark within a partial field, not a clean sweep of the whole city.

That leaves the landlord-profit numbers, which land the ward 47th out of 50. Eleven wards score close enough on this same measure that two points would gather in the entire group, so the bottom of this ranking is a crowd, not a clean last-place gap. A separate figure, how evenly the ward's yearly menu budget reaches its own blocks rather than clustering in one corner, ties back to boundaries that shifted in the 2023 redraw, so part of the historical trend behind that number reflects a ward that no longer exists in its old shape.

news.headline: Long-Delayed Plans For Bronzeville Pete's Fresh Market To Go Before City Panel Next Month
news.note: A developer plans to bring a grocery store, hardware store and apartments to the former Stateway Gardens site in Bronzeville, with a city Plan Commission hearing set for August 20.

news.headline: After Young People Shot In Bronzeville, Alder Calls For Accountability Over Teen Gatherings
news.note: Seven young people were shot in two separate incidents in Bronzeville over one weekend, prompting calls for parents and social media platforms to address unsanctioned teen gatherings.

news.headline: South Loop Neighbors Pitch New Bus Connector As Development Booms In Area
news.note: A community group proposed a 4.2-mile CTA bus route through the South Loop to ease congestion tied to nearby development, including the new Chicago Fire stadium.
